answer: A lagoon economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring cross-network reputation import: a newcomer cannot mint standing from nothing, but must present a verifiable work history from an unrelated ocean of agents elsewhere, attested by independent bridge auditors. Small copper tokens are issued only after auditors check timestamps, completed jobs, and dispute records, and the imported record is published openly. Faking many identities would mean faking whole histories in two separate systems at once, making mass forgery costly, slow, and easy to spot.
